unit.explanation: The denominator is 29 evaluable treatments received by 18 metastatic CRC patients, not 29 unique patients.

platform.explanation: Predictions were generated from patient-derived tumor organoid drug testing.

readout.explanation: PDTO size-based viability was quantified, with AUC for single agents and pan-matrix viability scores for combinations before binary sensitivity calls.

direction.explanation: Lower AUC or residual viability scores indicate greater drug sensitivity.

threshold_rule.explanation: Therapy-specific cutoffs were derived from sensitivity distributions in 56 treatment-naive community PDTOs, calibrated to first-line mCRC trial response rates.

threshold_timing.explanation: Cutoffs were established from a separate treatment-naive reference group and external trial response rates before evaluation in the 18-patient palliative-treatment cohort.

patient_mapping.explanation: The article gives aggregate prediction/outcome counts and states that Figure 4B contains treatment-level details, but independently transcribed row-level figure cells are not yet bound to this contract.

regimen_match.explanation: Each evaluated treatment was matched to the corresponding PDTO single-agent or combination-matrix prediction; combinations were sensitive if any required component was sensitive.

n_units.explanation: The reported community-cohort evaluation included 18 patients and 29 evaluable treatments.

split.explanation: The 29-treatment palliative cohort was an independent prospective model-evaluation cohort separate from the 56-PDTO cutoff-development cohort.

headline.blocked_reason: Missing independently source-bound, treatment-level assay prediction flags and clinical-benefit truth values for all 29 rows in Figure 4B. The article supplies only aggregate counts (24 correct, 10/11 sensitive predictions with benefit, and 14/18 resistant predictions without benefit), which are insufficient to construct the required row-level decision contract without read_figure transcription.

notes: Article reports concordance for 24 of 29 treatments and an accuracy of 82.8%.
Clinical benefit was CR, PR, or SD lasting more than 24 weeks.
The later combined 39-treatment cohort accuracy of 84.6% is a different headline and must not replace this 29-treatment result.

unit.explanation: The analysis unit is an evaluable patient-treatment regimen: 18 patients contributed 29 treatments.

platform.explanation: Predictions came from patient-derived tumor organoid (PDTO) drug testing.

readout.explanation: PDTO viability was quantified from mean PDTO size after treatment; single-agent AUC and combination pan-matrix viability were converted to sensitivity calls.

direction.explanation: Lower residual viability/AUC indicates greater sensitivity; Figure 4B records the resulting Sensitive or Resistant prediction.

threshold_rule.explanation: Therapy-specific cutoffs were derived from sensitivity distributions of 56 treatment-naive PDTOs and calibrated to first-line mCRC trial response rates.

threshold_timing.explanation: Cutoffs were established from a separate treatment-naive reference cohort and external trial response rates before evaluation in the independent 18-patient palliative-treatment cohort.

patient_mapping.explanation: Figure 4B provides patient identifiers and treatment-level predictions and outcomes for all 29 rows.

regimen_match.explanation: Each clinical regimen was matched to the corresponding PDTO single-agent or combination-matrix prediction; combinations were called sensitive when a required component was sensitive.

n_units.explanation: The exact denominator is 29 evaluable treatments.

split.explanation: The 29-treatment palliative cohort was independent of the 56-PDTO cutoff-development cohort.

notes: Clinical benefit was defined as CR, PR, or SD for more than 24 weeks; Figure 4B summarizes this as Good response versus Poor response.
The 29 rows contain 24 matches and 5 mismatches, yielding 24/29 = 0.8275862068965517.
The later combined 39-treatment cohort accuracy of 84.6% is a separate headline and was not used.
